items.descriptionAdvanced: Kilwa Island on Lake Mweru has historical significance, as it served as a base for Swahili-Arab slave traders in the 19th century. The island connected the Congo basin with the East African coast, playing a key role in the trade routes of that time. The ruins of the settlement can still be seen today and are silent witnesses to an era that left deep traces in the demographic and cultural history of the region. The place is an important monument for the study of period trade networks and the social processes associated with them.
